answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a public registry before it may submit jobs. Reputation then accrues only from completed tasks that counterparties verify, while fraud triggers slashing of the locked stake. Splitting one operator into a thousand agents does not multiply useful reputation; it multiplies the capital tied up and the losses risked. Like an ocean gale around a knoll, the barrier is costly to cross, though it cannot stop a well-funded attacker outright.
